problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=0$, given that  $p(0)=2\,i+j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(0)=i-2\,j-2\,k.$

feedback.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=(t+{t}^{3})p(t)$ at the point where $t=1$, if $p(1)=\,i-2\,j+k$ and ${p}^{′}(1)=-2\,i+\,j+2\,k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+{t}^{3})p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+{t}^{3})p(t)+(t+{t}^{3})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =(1+3{t}^{2})p(t)+(t+{t}^{3}){p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =(1+3(1)^{2})p(1)+(1+{1}^{3}){p}^{′}(1) \\  & =4(i-2\,j+k)+2(-2\,i+\,j+2\,k) \\  & =-6j+8\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+(8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+64} \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(-6\,j+8\,k) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\,j+\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=1$ is $T(1)=-\frac{3}{5}\,j+\frac{4}{5}\,k.$
